title: The Shop That Counted Returns
fact_notes: 人物・町・行事・数値や結果は架空の事例。実在の統計や研究結果ではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり、実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A small online store sold bags and other everyday items made by independent designers in the local area.
sentences.ja: 小さなオンライン店は地域の独立したデザイナーが作ったバッグなどの日用品を販売していた。

sentences.en: Its manager was pleased when monthly sales increased after a new advertising campaign attracted many first-time customers.
sentences.ja: 新しい広告活動が多くの初回客を呼び月間販売数が増え、店長は喜んだ。

sentences.en: However, the employee responsible for handling returned products noticed that her workload had increased considerably during the same period.
sentences.ja: しかし返品を処理する従業員は同時期に仕事量がかなり増えたことに気づいた。

sentences.en: She suggested examining the number of returns before deciding whether the campaign had been a complete success.
sentences.ja: 広告が完全に成功したか決める前に返品数を調べるよう提案した。

sentences.en: The manager initially regarded each completed sale as an important sign that the store was becoming more popular.
sentences.ja: 店長は当初、成立した販売一件一件を店の人気が高まる重要な指標と考えた。

sentences.en: Yet a returned item required another delivery, additional checking, and sometimes new packaging before it could be sold again.
sentences.ja: しかし返品された品は再販売前に別の配送、追加確認、ときに新たな梱包を必要とした。

sentences.en: Some bags were returned because their actual size differed from what customers had imagined after seeing the advertisement.
sentences.ja: 広告を見た客が想像していた大きさと実際の大きさが異なるため返品されたバッグもあった。

sentences.en: The store's photographs showed the products clearly but provided few clues about their dimensions in relation to familiar objects.
sentences.ja: 店の写真は商品を鮮明に示したが、身近な物と比べた寸法の手がかりはほとんどなかった。

sentences.en: Instead of immediately increasing the advertising budget, the employees revised the pages displaying the most frequently returned items.
sentences.ja: すぐ広告予算を増やす代わりに、従業員は返品頻度の高い商品のページを修正した。

sentences.en: They included measurements in a more visible position and added pictures showing bags beside ordinary notebooks and water bottles.
sentences.ja: 寸法をより目立つ位置に掲載し、普通のノートや水筒の横にバッグを置いた写真も加えた。

sentences.en: They also explained which products were suitable for carrying a laptop and which were intended for smaller personal belongings.
sentences.ja: ノートパソコンの持ち運びに適した商品と、小物向けの商品も説明した。

sentences.en: The changes were designed to help potential customers make more informed choices, even if some decided against buying anything.
sentences.ja: 一部の人が購入をやめるとしても、見込み客がより情報に基づいた選択をできるように変更した。

sentences.en: During the following month, the manager tracked completed sales, returns, delivery expenses, and customer comments instead of sales alone.
sentences.ja: 翌月、店長は販売数だけでなく、成立した販売、返品、配送費、客の意見を追跡した。

sentences.en: The revised pages received fewer complaints about size, although the store also introduced other changes during that month.
sentences.ja: 修正ページは大きさへの苦情が減ったが、店は同じ月に別の変更も導入した。

sentences.en: The manager therefore avoided claiming that the photographs alone had caused every improvement in the store's overall performance.
sentences.ja: そのため写真だけが店の業績のすべての改善を引き起こしたとは主張しなかった。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the additional records helped the team identify previously hidden costs and discuss how to serve customers more effectively.
sentences.ja: それでも追加記録は隠れていた費用を見つけ、より効果的に顧客に対応する方法を考える助けとなった。

sentences.en: The employees realized that attracting a potential buyer and satisfying a customer were related but distinct business goals.
sentences.ja: 従業員は見込み客を呼び込むことと顧客を満足させることは関連するが異なる事業目標だと気づいた。

sentences.en: A measurement of success becomes more useful when it includes the outcomes that matter beyond the first transaction.
sentences.ja: 成功の尺度は最初の取引の後にも重要な結果を含めるとより有用になる。

sentences.en: For this store, a slightly lower number of unsuitable purchases might be preferable to a larger number of disappointing experiences.
sentences.ja: この店では不適切な購入が少し減る方が、がっかりする体験が多いより望ましい場合がある。

sentences.en: Its most important discovery was that the quality of a sale deserved as much attention as the quantity of sales.
sentences.ja: 最大の発見は販売の質にも販売数と同程度の注意を払う価値があることだった。

questions.prompt: What initially pleased the store manager?
options: The designers had closed their businesses.

questions.prompt: What did the returns employee notice?
options: The shop had stopped receiving orders.
All customers bought the same bag.
The advertising campaign had ended before it started.
questions.explanation_ja: 返品処理の仕事量が増加した。

questions.prompt: Why can a return increase business costs?
options: It always requires creating a new advertisement.
It removes the need for packaging.
It involves extra transport and handling.
questions.explanation_ja: 配送や点検など追加費用が生じる。

options: They were not the size customers had imagined.
They had been sent to the designers instead.
They had all been advertised at different prices.
They were missing a legally required label.
questions.explanation_ja: 想像と実際の大きさが異なった。

questions.prompt: What did the employees add to product pages?
options: Pictures comparing bags with familiar objects.
questions.explanation_ja: 身近な物と並べた写真を掲載。

questions.prompt: Why might clearer descriptions lead some visitors not to buy?
options: The product pages would no longer show any images.
Customers would be banned from comparing products.
The shop would refuse every first-time customer.
They may realize a product does not fit their needs.
questions.explanation_ja: 用途に合わないと判断する客もいる。

questions.prompt: What did the manager measure in the following month?
options: Sales, returns, delivery costs, and comments.
The number of designers in the town.
questions.explanation_ja: 複数の指標を追跡した。

questions.prompt: Why did the manager avoid crediting photographs alone for all improvements?
options: No product pages had actually been revised.
The store had lost all its records.
Other changes had also been made.
questions.explanation_ja: 同月中に別の変更もあり因果を確定できない。
関連するが異なるという意味。

questions.prompt: What is the author's main point?
options: A store should accept every purchase without question.
Business success should consider what happens after a sale as well as sales volume.
Advertising is the only meaningful business investment.
A customer return always proves dishonest advertising.
questions.explanation_ja: 販売後の結果と販売数の両方を評価する。

grammar.focus: before it could be sold again
grammar.explanation_ja: before節は再販売に先立つ処理を示す。
whatは〜するもの・ことという名詞節を導く。

grammar.focus: even if some decided against buying anything
grammar.explanation_ja: even ifは仮定的な譲歩を示す。
過去完了は主張時点以前の原因を表す。

discourse.role_ja: 販売増加と返品業務増加を対比する。
販売後の追加費用を示す。
広告費増加ではなく情報改善を選んだ。
因果の限界があっても記録に価値があったことを示す。

paraphrases.source: Yet a returned item required another delivery, additional checking, and sometimes new packaging before it could be sold again.
paraphrases.rewrite: A product sent back to the shop needed another shipment and examination before becoming available again.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 返品後に追加処理が必要。

paraphrases.source: Some bags were returned because their actual size differed from what customers had imagined after seeing the advertisement.
paraphrases.rewrite: Customers returned certain bags because the real size did not match their expectations from the advertisement.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 広告から想像した大きさと違っていた。

paraphrases.source: The changes were designed to help potential customers make more informed choices, even if some decided against buying anything.
paraphrases.rewrite: The aim was to let shoppers make better-informed decisions, including deciding not to purchase.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 買わない選択も含め情報に基づく判断を助ける。

paraphrases.source: The manager therefore avoided claiming that the photographs alone had caused every improvement in the store's overall performance.
paraphrases.rewrite: The manager did not attribute all the better results solely to the new images.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 写真だけに改善を帰属させなかった。

cloze.explanation_ja: 返品には梱包などの費用が必要。
大きさへの苦情が減った。
販売数だけでなく質も重視。
